intended_object: The canonical k-linear isomorphism Γ(X, 𝒦_X) ≅ K(X) for an integral scheme X over Spec k: the global sections of the sheaf of rational functions are the function field (from the docstring and the module context).
explanation: The body reuses the library's identification `rationalFunctionsEquiv ⊤` of the sections of 𝒦_X over a nonempty open with K(X). 𝒦_X is the pushforward of 𝒪 along Spec K(X) → X, and the identification is Γ(X,⊤)-linear. The open ⊤ is nonempty because an integral scheme is irreducible, hence nonempty. The body then checks that the k-action agrees on both sides: on global sections k acts through the map k → Γ(X,⊤), and on K(X) it acts through algebraMap k K(X), the germ at the generic point of the image of k. So this is exactly the canonical isomorphism, made k-linear. The generality is natural: K(X) is a field only for integral X, 𝒦_X as defined needs X irreducible, and k is an arbitrary commutative ring. Mathlib has the function field but no sheaf of rational functions, so it has no counterpart to this isomorphism.
